answers.explanation: Unlike radio, which spreads in all directions, microwaves go one way.
That's why microwave antennas go on tall towers: to see over obstacles and the curve of the Earth.
Terrestrial goes tower to tower across land. Satellite goes up to a satellite and back down.
Microwaves span 1 to 300 GHz, but 3 to 30 GHz is the usual range.
Atmospheric conditions are one of microwave's listed disadvantages.
The opposite: physical obstacles can interrupt the beam.
Infrared fades fast and is blocked by anything in the way.
Short range and line of sight suit a TV remote perfectly.
The same property that limits it also contains it.
